# Pandamonium v1.0.37

Browse pinned tasks and projects in your preferred order, inspect session context, and choose native Codex reasoning or a bounded Jarvis work budget from the conversation picker.

## MAD-869 — Workspace UI: restore pins, custom ordering, session details, and effort controls

### Problem

Friday omitted Codex desktop pins and ordering, and long task lists used nested scrollers. Dragging ordinary chats inside folders did not save their order. Refreshing the identity picker could clear a selected Codex task. Session environment and activity were not visible beside the conversation.

### Implementation

The private bridge reads native project order through App Server and narrowly reads desktop-only pin/task-order hints. All task metadata and recent activity come from App Server with exact allowlisted project checks. Pandamonium stores subsequent layout changes in owner preferences. Project and recent chats show five rows at a time; each Show more click adds five. Drag handles and Alt + Up/Down reorder rows without changing the task's working directory. Slow sidebar loads cannot replace an explicit task selection, and picker refresh preserves the selected Codex task.

The Details panel shows available environment, sources, tools, and outputs. The model picker contains native supported Codex reasoning efforts and Jarvis's separately labeled Agent work budget. Jarvis levels cap model/tool rounds at 8, 12, 20, 40, or 80 while retaining early completion and existing authority, tool-budget, and verification checks. The service worker is advanced to load the new UI module.

### Product value and UI visibility

Pinned tasks appear above Projects. Select a project, reveal five more tasks at a time, or reorder rows with their handles or keyboard shortcuts. Open the conversation picker to choose a Codex model and effort or Jarvis work budget. Open Details for recorded environment and recent activity; the panel collapses when opening the picker on narrow screens.

### Verification

Focused bridge tests exercise native layout order, pin allowlisting, safe metadata projection, and refusal to read another project's activity. Browser checks exercise pins, five-row expansion, saved pointer/keyboard order, model and budget propagation, task retention after picker refresh, and narrow-screen layout. A clean authenticated running app read all 27 configured workstation projects, the desktop pin, and actual recorded model/branch/tool metadata through a separate read-only bridge. Unauthenticated detail requests returned 401. The full Python suite passed 5,545 tests with 5 intentional skips. All 88 browser regression tests passed. JavaScript syntax, Python compilation, service-worker transition checks, and diff hygiene passed.

### Configuration, compatibility, and limitations

Update Pandamonium and its private PC bridge together. Existing credentials and workspace aliases remain unchanged. Codex continues to run on the workstation with its existing global/project instruction hierarchy; no database copying, schema change, dependency, or second agent loop is introduced. Desktop layout is the initial source; Pandamonium changes are saved independently and do not write back to Codex. The right panel lists recent recorded activity: the latest five Codex turns or latest 50 Pandamonium messages. Recorded branch/model values are not a live Git status check. Jarvis work budget applies to the next text turn; voice retains its existing budget. Higher limits permit more work but do not force rounds or increase a model's native reasoning capability. The separate MCP response/recovery failure in MAD-842 remains unresolved by this UI release.
